sara: quick sync — ran a tiny prefill/entropy probe on the new 13B q4f model this morning. objective was to drop prefill tokens when prefix entropy < 1.2 to save decode ops. results: ~12% median token latency reduction but BLEU/QA hits on short-answer sets (SQuAD slices) — total exact match dropped ~5pts. :confused:

mike: can you paste the exact command/config you used? curious about batching + kv warmups.

sara: run (condensed):
```
python infra/run_decode.py \
  --model redwood/13b-q4f \
  --mode speculative_prefill \
  --prefill-entropy-threshold 1.2 \
  --batch-size 8 \
  --kv-warmup true 
```
metrics dump: median_token_latency_ms: 21 -> 18.4, p95: 78 -> 70, EM(SQuAD_short): 82 -> 77. token-savings estimated ~9% total tokens per request.

anita: interesting. did you isolate short prompts vs long-context? prefill dropout tends to bias the model if early tokens are informative.

sara: yeah split by prompt len: short (<40 tokens) saw most QA EM drop, long (>200 tokens) had negligible EM change and best latency wins.

mike: did you re-calibrate sampling/temp? sometimes lower entropy threshold acts like temperature shift because you effectively truncate stochastic mass.

sara: sampling unchanged (topk=50, temp=0.8). I think it’s mostly prefix info loss when we skip prefill tokens — KV cache miss changes conditioning.

anita: suggestion: try a two-tier rule: for short prompts require one token warmup regardless of entropy; for long prompts allow entropy-based skip. Then measure per-bucket QA and perplexity. Also run n-gram overlap and answer-span length distribution.

ci-bot: test run scheduled: job/4523 started (compare/13b-q4f/prefill-vs-baseline). link: https://console.redwood/internal/runs/4523 :gear:

mike: also test with 4-bit per-tensor quant vs q4f layout — quantization layout can amplify small distributional shifts.

sara: ack — spinning q4f vs q4_0 now. will post a tiny table when done. for now flagging this as "quality-risk: short prompt QA" for the spec-decode checklist. :eyes:

anita: add an eval that uses short, factual QA + instruction-follow slices (50/50) so we catch both hallucination and exact-match regressions.

sara: will do. next update ~ in 2h after q4_0 run. thanks! :thumbsup:
